summary: An excerpt from a novel's Book 10 in which Lee-Daniel, a company founder, is pressed by Mac and the company's leadership to stay on during a leadership transition at CogRad. The scene opens with a network relay problem during a live event, where Lee-Daniel's staff pass messages down a chain of people, and Lee-Daniel shows his authority. Mac then argues that Lee-Daniel is needed to train his successor and will profit from a planned IPO and expansion, while Lee-Daniel privately doubts Mac's sincerity. The excerpt ends mid-speech as Mac promises a big payoff.
one_line: Lee-Daniel, ousted from his company CogRad, is persuaded by Mac to stay on through a transition while investors watch and an IPO looms.
key_facts: Lee-Daniel is the speaker in a scene where he explains a network relay problem involving radios and a choice between waiting or finding an alternate path.
The switchgirl is a network engineer Lee-Daniel hired from a backwater DeVry at a job-fair in Tulsa.
The switchgirl ran a little to fat but was still broad-shouldered from her time on the rowing machine she shlepped from gig to gig.
Joey Riel was by the doorway and stuck his head into the corridor to relay the message.
Mortimer boomed into the mic from the auditorium, asking "You want something, boss?"
Mac asks Lee-Daniel "So, what's the critical path" and asks who will run the company between that night and the arrival of an executive search.
Mac tells Lee-Daniel "We thought you'd stay on, LD, help with a smooth transition."
The Series A and Series B investors watched the exchange silently, eyes shining, like spectators at a tennis match.
Lee-Daniel suspects Mac is blowing smoke and massaging his ego.
Lee-Daniel reflects that CogRad is no longer his company: "Not his company, not anymore."
Mac says "they don't want you to stay" and that he had to fight hard to keep Lee-Daniel in during the transition.
Mac claims Lee-Daniel is the only one who can train his successor because the job cannot be filled by a warm body.
Mac says Lee-Daniel can retire on his share in 18 months if the plan goes as expected.
Mac plans to franchise the business, start new busses, and turn the product into a turnkey solution that scales.
Mac predicts CogRad will raise 10 billion on IPO "if we raise a cent."
